annotations.text:
THE MOVE THAT MATTERS — stop describing the three growths, and show them.

A person at a streambank cannot separate filamentous algae from a cyanobacterial bloom from sewage fungus by reading three sentences, and a wrong call either way means a missed pollution incident or a false alarm. So every direction draws the specimens. The illustration is the feature, not decoration.

All four artboards carry identical copy, lifted verbatim from backend/domain/field_protocol.py, and identical specimen geometry from design/specimens.py. Design is the only variable.

The drawings are schematic aids shown beside the descriptions — not authoritative identification plates. They have not been validated against real field examples, and that is worth an ecologist's hour before launch.

RECOMMENDATION CHANGED — now Broadsheet, not Cyanotype.

GPT reviewed all three independently and picked Broadsheet, rejecting the Cyanotype recommendation. Its decisive argument: two of the three surfaces still to build are dense reviewer UI — a triage queue and a detail view with four assessment dimensions — and that is where a strong aesthetic breaks. A light ground with a sans body extends there; an ornate dark plate does not.

It also found the defect that settled it: the options name COLOURS — green strands, blue-green like spilled paint, grey or dirty-white slime — and every direction drew all three in one ink, discarding the first thing a person matches. Specimens are now drawn in their own colours, with shape still distinct so the reading survives colour blindness and greyscale.

And that disqualifies Cyanotype on its own terms: a cyanotype is monochrome by process. Its concept structurally forbids the single most diagnostic feature. The concept fights the function.

NOW — what is deployed.

Tailwind defaults and the three options as plain text rows. Competent and forgettable.

Shown with the same copy as the others so the comparison is fair.

1 · CYANOTYPE — no longer recommended.

Anna Atkins' 1843 process: Prussian blue plate, white photograms, EB Garamond, the chosen option pulled as a positive print.

Why it lost: it is monochrome by definition, so it cannot show the colour that identifies the growth. GPT also judged the Atkins reference a liability — freshwater expertise does not imply photographic-history recognition, and claiming the reference confers scientific standing reads as pretension. Keep it as a one-line design credit at most.

Still the most beautiful of the three. That is not the same as the most useful.

2 · NOCTURNE

Dark water optics, luminous specimens, Space Grotesk, mint signal and amber alarm.

Why it lost: GPT called the caustics decoration rather than evidence of field suitability, and it is right — the dawn/dusk justification was thin, and the middle of the screen renders flat anyway.

A dark ground also makes the reviewer queue harder, not easier.

3 · BROADSHEET — recommended.

A field observation sheet. Newsprint, Bodoni Moda masthead and headline, Archivo for everything you actually read, one red reserved for the precaution.

Now carrying GPT's five corrections: 'Field observation' rather than 'Water notice', so a citizen report does not masquerade as an official warning; an explicit 'Your answer' with a check instead of an inverted black row; 'Awaiting review' beside the reading; body text up to 15px; paper grain removed.

Strongest hierarchy at a glance, and the only one whose type and ground extend cleanly into a dense reviewer queue.

Say the word and I will build Broadsheet through capture, review queue and reviewer detail, then move on to P4.

If you prefer Cyanotype on looks, say so and I will build it — but the colour problem is real, and I would want to solve it before committing (probably by keeping the blue plate for chrome and letting the specimens alone carry colour).
